prediction.likelyOutcome: The court will most likely reject full rent acceleration and apply a deficiency measure under Section 10.02(b), crediting relet income, while awarding little to nothing on the $300,000 kitchen claim given LBJ Venture's failure to prove value or enhancement at trial; attorneys' fees will be awarded but likely trimmed from the requested $67,000 to reflect the landlord's partial success. Net result: a judgment materially closer to Kolaj's ~$96,000 counter-calculation than to LBJ Venture's ~$905,000 combined request, though with a realistic chance the court credits the landlord's acceleration theory and pushes the award substantially higher.

issues.label: Rent Damages: Acceleration vs. Deficiency Under Section 10.02(b)

outcome.description: After the bench trial the trial court rendered judgment for the landlord of $96,072.49 (unpaid rent through trial net of replacement-tenant rent, late fees, and prejudgment interest) — the figure the tenant advocated, roughly one-tenth of the more than $900,000 the landlord sought — plus 18% post-judgment interest, and awarded $0 in attorneys' fees. The court of appeals affirmed the damages award and reversed only the denial of attorneys' fees, remanding for a determination of a reasonable fee under the lease.
outcome.finalNote: Damages affirmed; fee denial reversed and remanded.
